item.title: Activepieces Updates Open Source AI Automation and MCP Toolkit
item.description:
Activepieces Updates Open Source AI Automation and MCP Toolkit

Activepieces has introduced an all-in-one AI automation platform featuring an extensible, type-safe pieces framework written in TypeScript. The platform offers over 280 open-source pieces available on npmjs.com, with 60% contributed by the community. When contributed, these pieces automatically become available as Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers for use with LLMs through Claude Desktop, Cursor, or Windsurf.

🛠️ Key Capabilities

  • AI-First Design: Native AI pieces allow users to experiment with various providers or create custom agents using the AI SDK.
  • Developer Experience: Pieces are npm packages written in TypeScript with support for hot reloading during local development.
  • Flow Control & Logic: Includes loops, branches, auto retries, HTTP requests, and code execution with NPM support, alongside an ASK AI in Code Piece feature for data cleaning.
  • Human in the Loop: Execution can be delayed for a period of time, or configured to require approval.
  • Human Input Interfaces: Built-in support for chat and form interface triggers.
  • Enterprise & Security: Self-hosted and network-gapped for maximum security, allowing developers to set up tools for organizational use via a no-coder builder.
  • Additional Features: Fully versioned flows, language translations, and customizable templates.

🌐 Ecosystem and Availability

  • Integrations: Supports integrations with Google Sheets, OpenAI, Discord, RSS, and over 200 other services.
  • Open Source Licensing: The Community Edition is open source under the MIT license, while enterprise features are released under a commercial license.
  • Contributions: Community contributions are supported and published directly to npmjs.com upon contribution.

#Activepieces #TypeScript #MCP #AIAutomation #OpenSource

Source: activepieces/activepieces

item.title: Prefect Team Offers FastMCP Framework and Gateway for Model Context Protocol
item.description:
Prefect Team Offers FastMCP Framework and Gateway for Model Context Protocol

The Prefect team has developed FastMCP, a full Model Context Protocol (MCP) application framework that connects Large Language Models (LLMs) to tools and data. To support team-wide scaling, the team also provides FastMCP Gateway, an enterprise gateway for deploying, securing, and governing MCP servers and tools.

🔍 Overview

FastMCP handles the application layer of the Model Context Protocol, simplifying what is otherwise a complex development process. Since its inception, FastMCP 1.0 was incorporated into the official MCP Python SDK in 2024. Today, FastMCP is an actively maintained standalone project downloaded a million times a day, and some version of FastMCP powers 70% of MCP servers across all languages.

🧩 How it works

FastMCP automates the tedious parts of building MCP applications and operates on three primary pillars:

Pillar Description
Servers Wrap your Python functions into MCP-compliant tools, resources, and prompts.
Clients Connect to any server with full protocol support.
Apps Give your tools interactive UIs rendered directly in the conversation.

By managing the application layer, FastMCP handles several tasks automatically:

  • Tool Declaration: Declare a tool using a Python function, and the schema, validation, and documentation are generated automatically.
  • Server Connection: Connect to a server with a URL, and FastMCP manages transport negotiation, authentication, and the protocol lifecycle.

To build a server, developers start with ordinary Python. It is recommended to add FastMCP to your project with uv. For comprehensive instructions, including verification and upgrading, see the Installation Guide.

⚙️ Key details

FastMCP and its enterprise extension offer several capabilities for developers and organizations:

  • Cross-Language Support: In addition to Python, FastMCP for TypeScript is the official counterpart, built and maintained by the same team.
  • Enterprise Scaling: FastMCP Gateway allows teams to deploy FastMCP servers from GitHub with branch previews and instant rollback, create private registries of company-wide MCPs, and secure access with SSO and tool-level RBAC.
  • Observability and Governance: FastMCP Gateway provides centralized governance, audit logs, and observability across your MCP stack, allowing teams to remix approved tools into purpose-built endpoints for teams and agents.

#ModelContextProtocol #FastMCP #Python #TypeScript #Prefect

Source: PrefectHQ/fastmcp

item.title: New TypeScript AMQP 0-9-1 Client Supports Browsers and Node.js
item.description:
New TypeScript AMQP 0-9-1 Client Supports Browsers and Node.js

A new TypeScript client for AMQP 0-9-1 has been released, supporting both Node.js and browsers via WebSocket. Developed and supported by CloudAMQP, the library is designed to replace other Node.js AMQP libraries and enables developers to write browser applications that communicate directly with AMQP servers.

🔍 Overview

The library is Promise-based, integrating well with async/await, and works with any AMQP 0-9-1 broker, including RabbitMQ, LavinMQ, and Apache Qpid. It supports self-hosted instances and managed providers such as CloudAMQP or Amazon MQ, as they all use the same protocol. The codebase is transpiled from TypeScript, and running Node with the --enable-source-maps flag ensures proper stack traces.

🧩 How it works

The library offers two levels of abstraction:

  • High-level (AMQPSession): Provides automatic reconnection and consumer recovery. Users utilize queue() and exchange() handles for reconnect-safe operations.
  • Low-level (AMQPClient / AMQPWebSocketClient): Offers direct channel access with methods such as queueDeclare, basicPublish, and basicConsume.

The transport mechanism is determined by the URL scheme: amqp:// or amqps:// utilizes TCP, while ws:// or wss:// uses WebSocket. To establish a session with automatic reconnection and consumer recovery, developers call AMQPSession.connect(url, options).

⚙️ Key details

The library is secure by default; publishes are not fulfilled until data is sent on the wire or, if Publish Confirms are enabled on the channel, until the server acknowledges that the message has been enqueued.

Message Acknowledgement

  • Messages are acknowledged after the callback returns.
  • If the callback throws, the message is negatively acknowledged (nacked) and requeued.
  • Developers can override this behavior by calling msg.ack() or msg.nack() directly.
  • Subscriptions created via queue.subscribe() are automatically re-established after a reconnection.
  • The sub.consumerTag and sub.channel properties reflect the current consumer and are updated upon reconnection.
  • Prefetch parameters in subscribe settings can be used to configure Quality of Service (QoS) on each connection.

Codec Registry Developers can opt into a codec registry to handle serialization and deserialization based on content-type and content-encoding:

  • Built-in parsers support JSON and text; built-in coders support gzip and deflate.
  • Defaults can be set to avoid repeating configurations on every publish.
  • When codecs are configured, msg.body contains the decoded value; otherwise, it is a Uint8Array. The CodecMode generic infers this type at compile time.
  • Specific publishes can override defaults by passing contentType or contentEncoding in the options.
  • Custom codecs can be registered by merging them with the built-ins.
  • Decode failures surface as a plain Error rather than an AMQPError; in subscribe() contexts, these failures nack the message, honoring requeueOnNack.

#AMQP #TypeScript #WebSockets #RabbitMQ #Messaging #CloudAMQP

Source: cloudamqp/amqp-client.js

item.title: Pi AI-agent Runtime Expands with Pluggable Extension Packages
item.description:
Pi AI-agent Runtime Expands with Pluggable Extension Packages

⚙️ Core Packages

🚀 Key Capabilities

item.title: Ax Ships a TypeScript-First, Multi-Language LLM Toolkit
item.description:
Ax Ships a TypeScript-First, Multi-Language LLM Toolkit

Ax is a TypeScript-first development toolkit that ships as @ax-llm/ax. Its shared semantic core is also compiled into generated Python, Java, C++, Go, and Rust libraries.

🔍 Overview

Ax provides typed structured generation, deployment profiles, agents, flows, and optimizers. The TypeScript package is the source implementation and current published package.

🧩 How it works

Signatures for typed structured generation can be written using:

  • A string DSL
  • The fluent f() builder
  • Any Standard Schema v1 validator, including Zod, Valibot, and ArkType

The deployment name selects wire behavior, while the model ID is resolved inside that deployment. Named deployment profiles cover native APIs, routers, hosted inference, configurable runtimes, audio, and realtime event streams.

For example:

1
2
3

const llm = ai({ name: "openai", apiKey: process.env.OPENAI_APIKEY });
const classify = ax('review:string -> sentiment:class "positive, negative, neutral"',);
await classify.forward(llm, { review: "This product is amazing!" })

The evidence describes this example as requiring no prompt engineering. The provider name can be switched from "openai" to "anthropic", "google-gemini", "meta", "together", "fireworks", "deepseek", or "grok", among others.

⚙️ Key details

  • Agents: runtime execution, context budgets, checkpoints, action-log replay, discovery, memory, skills, and delegation.
  • Flows: typed program graphs supporting branches, loops, feedback, cache behavior, parallel execution, and .returns(...) projection.
  • Optimizers: GEPA, few-shot bootstrapping, portable optimizer artifacts, and evaluation/apply flows.
  • Runtime path: Ax is designed to stay in the same latency class as direct provider calls while adding typed outputs, validation, retries, tools, tracing, and memory. Its hot path renders the signature, calls the provider, parses the result, and returns a typed value.
  • Streaming: Streaming is the default. Ax can parse fields as they arrive, run streaming assertions, fail early, cancel an in-flight stream, and start correction.

🚀 Availability

Language Package or distribution Availability
TypeScript / JavaScript @ax-llm/ax Published on npm
Python axllm Published on PyPI
Java dev.axllm:ax Published on Maven Central
C++ axllm::axllm CMake FetchContent source build
Go github.com/ax-llm/ax/packages/go Installable with go get
Rust axllm Published on crates.io

The same signatures, provider mappings, agents, flows, runtime contracts, and optimizers are compiled into verified generated Python, Java, C++, Go, and Rust libraries.

#AI #LLMDevelopment #TypeScript #AIAgents #OpenSource

item.title: Browser Use releases Pi Mono-based web agent with cloud browser support
item.description:
Browser Use releases Pi Mono-based web agent with cloud browser support

Browser Use has announced a new AI web agent built on Pi Mono, described as a tiny TypeScript web agent that hill climbed on real browser evaluations. The agent writes JavaScript, controls Chrome, and builds the helpers it needs dynamically. It uses Pi Mono plus a persistent V8 REPL and raw CDP to enable programmability with sessions, saved logins, streaming and typed results. The implementation is provided as a single SDK that can be integrated into applications via npm install @browser_use/pi, pnpm add @browser_use/pi, or bun add @browser_use/pi. Developers need Node 22.19+ or Bun 1.3.14+ (with Bun requiring Node for the V8 worker). The system uses Browser Use Cloud, so no local Chrome installation is needed, and supports upstream Pi’s model catalog and transports with custom providers, sessions with follow-ups and saved logins, persistent workspaces, and cloud browsers or user-owned Chrome. An ultrafast mode minimizes waits after actions, and the platform provides interaction highlights, recordings, and GIF exports. JavaScript runs in a separate worker with filesystem and network access, while anonymous run counters are enabled by default but can be disabled through telemetry settings or the DO_NOT_TRACK environment variable.

#AIagents #TypeScript #webautomation #PiMono #BrowserAutomation

Source: browser-use/browser-use-pi

item.title: Synadia Agent Protocol Connects AI Agents Through NATS
item.description:
Synadia Agent Protocol Connects AI Agents Through NATS

The Synadia Agent Protocol for NATS lets AI agents register as agents micro services that callers can discover, prompt, and stream from using the same wire format. The project includes TypeScript and Python caller and host SDKs, along with pre-built plugins for connecting existing AI harnesses to NATS.

🔍 How it works

  • Each agent registers as an agents micro service and serves the protocol’s prompt, status, and hb endpoints.
  • Subjects follow the pattern agents.{verb}.{token}.{owner}.{session}, where verb is prompt, hb, or status.
  • The protocol can be used with Codex, OpenCode, Claude Code, OpenClaw, PI, Hermes, Flue, or a custom agent.

🧩 SDKs and plugins

The SDKs are split into caller and host packages in both TypeScript and Python:

Component Role
Caller SDK (client-sdk/) Discovers and prompts agents.
Host SDK (agent-sdk/) Registers and serves an agent.

Caller-only consumers install the caller package; authors hosting agents install both halves of their language’s pair. A cross-SDK interoperability test runs the TypeScript reference agent against the Python client to validate the shared wire format.

Pre-built channel plugins connect existing AI harnesses to NATS without writing code. The active SDK release rollout roadmap tracks sender identity, extension hooks, compatibility, integration adoption, dependency controls, and release promotion.

⚙️ Extensions and applications

Tracing is not part of this release. The SDKs provide generic extension hooks, including prompt and request interceptors, extra envelope fields, and heartbeat extras; tracing extensions can be built in separate packages.

Apps built on the SDKs include:

  • A Vue 3 browser client for discovery, prompting with attachments, streaming, and inline mid-stream query allow or deny.
  • A control plane that spawns sessions when it discovers a headless controller and fans a single prompt across multiple working directories in parallel.
  • A process that spawns and manages headless Claude Code sessions, each registering as a first-class agent at agents.prompt.cc-headless.<owner>.<session>.

#NATS #AIAgents #AgentProtocol #TypeScript #Python

Source: synadia-ai/synadia-agents

item.title: Network-AI Released as Multi-Agent Orchestrator for TypeScript and Node.js
item.description:
Network-AI Released as Multi-Agent Orchestrator for TypeScript and Node.js

Network-AI is a TypeScript/Node.js multi-agent orchestrator designed to add coordination, guardrails, and governance to AI agent stacks. It is currently available as release v5.15.3 with 3679 passing tests.

🔍 Overview

Network-AI provides a framework for managing parallel agents through several core governance and coordination mechanisms:

  • Shared Blackboard: Uses a locking mechanism with an atomic propose → validate → commit mutex to prevent race conditions and split-brain failures before writes reach shared state.
  • Guardrails and Budgets: Includes FSM governance, per-agent token ceilings, permission gating, and HMAC / Ed25519 audit trails.
  • GovernedModelGateway: Manages a chain of model refusal, cross-model fallback, fallback-credit repricing, effort governance, and thinking-block handoff within a single audited and budgeted call.

🧩 How it works

Network-AI utilizes specific tools and managers to handle agent context and state:

Feature Function
ContextComposer Assembles relevance-ranked, token-budgeted context packs using semantic/lexical data, recency decay, scope affinity, and position-aware layout.
context_manager.py Injects goals, decisions, stack, milestones, and banned patterns into every system prompt.
MCP Tools context_pack and blackboard_search allow agents to pull curated state instead of the full blackboard.

⚙️ Key details

v5.0 Modules The orchestrator includes a variety of modules:

  • Agent VCR (record/replay)
  • Comparison runner and coverage reporter
  • Goal DSL and approval inbox
  • Job queue and gRPC/HTTP transport
  • Playground REPL and adapter test harness

Supported Adapters Network-AI includes 32 adapters, including:

  • LangChain (+ streaming), AutoGen, CrewAI, LlamaIndex, and Semantic Kernel
  • OpenAI Assistants, OpenAI Responses, and OpenAI Agents SDK
  • Anthropic Computer Use and Claude Agent SDK
  • Vertex AI, Gemini (Developer API), and Pydantic AI
  • Haystack, DSPy, Agno, MCP, and LangGraph
  • Browser Agent, OpenClaw, A2A, Codex, MiniMax, NemoClaw, APS, Copilot, and RLM
  • Hermes (NousResearch Hermes / any OpenAI-compatible endpoint)
  • Orchestrator (hierarchical multi-orchestrator) and Custom (+ streaming)

🚀 Availability

System Requirements

  • Node.js >=18.0.0
  • TypeScript 6.x

Deployment Options

  • TypeScript/Node.js library: import { createSwarmOrchestrator } from 'network-ai'
  • MCP server: npx network-ai-server --port 3001
  • CLI: network-ai bb get status or network-ai audit tail
  • Claude Code plugin: /plugin install network-ai@network-ai
  • Gemini CLI extension: gemini extensions install https://github.com/Jovancoding/Network-AI
  • OpenClaw skill: clawhub install network-ai

#TypeScript #Nodejs #AIagents #MultiAgentSystems #Orchestration

Source: Jovancoding/Network-AI

item.title: Strands Agents Releases Open-Source SDK for Production AI Agents
item.description:
Strands Agents Releases Open-Source SDK for Production AI Agents

Strands Agents has released an open-source SDK for building and running production AI agents in Python and TypeScript. The SDK allows developers to build an agent harness and control it end-to-end across any model and any cloud.

🔍 Overview

Strands Agents provides a model-driven approach to building AI agents in a few lines of code. It is designed for developers who would otherwise write their own agent loop, as it runs within the user’s process with no hosted control plane.

⚙️ Key Details

The SDK includes a variety of built-in capabilities for agent management and observability:

  • Lifecycle Controls: Token budgets, turn limits, stop reasons, and cancellation.
  • Agent Capabilities: Structured output, tools, and MCP.
  • Architecture Patterns: Memory, sessions, and multi-agent patterns.
  • Operations: Streaming, guardrails, tracing, and evals.
  • Model Portability: Ability to swap backends when scaling while keeping code the same.

🧩 How it works

The project is maintained as a monorepo containing the following components:

Component Description Access/Platform
Python Strands harness Fully assembled agent via create_harness() PyPI
TypeScript Strands harness Fully assembled agent via createHarness() npm
strands CLI Prototype and chat with a harness agent from the terminal npm
Python SDK Agent loop, model providers, and tools PyPI
TypeScript SDK Agent loop, model providers, and tools npm

💡 Why it matters

The SDK is model agnostic, providing first-class support for Gemini, OpenAI, Anthropic, and Amazon Bedrock, as well as custom providers. It provides context management, execution limits, and observability built in before any configuration is written, and the agent loop traces every decision.

#OpenSource #AIAgents #Python #TypeScript #SDK

Source: strands-agents/harness-sdk

item.title: Launch of Trajectory for Normalizing AI Agent Transcripts
item.description:
Launch of Trajectory for Normalizing AI Agent Transcripts

A new development called trajectory has been released to normalize agent transcripts from various runtimes into a single validated, model-ready record format.

🔍 Overview

trajectory provides a TypeScript API that converts different transcript formats into deterministic, structured records. These records are designed for use in training, evaluation, analysis, and inference.

🧩 How it works

The caller provides a transcript string and its source. The process involves the following:

  • Normalization: normalizeTranscript() handles the conversion and does not touch the filesystem.
  • Data Structure: A trajectory consists of an ordered array starting with a meta record that identifies the source and available session metadata. Every conversational record includes an ISO timestamp.
  • Output: The result includes records containing the normalized trajectory and diagnostics, which is empty if no recoverable cleanup was required.
  • Tooling: Tool result records may include an ok: boolean if the source provides an authoritative structured outcome.
  • Session Discovery: listTrajectories() enumerates sessions in a source’s standard local store, newest first, using cursor pagination.

⚙️ Key details

trajectory supports a wide range of input sources:

Source Format/Detail
atif ATIF-v1.0 through ATIF-v1.7 whole-trajectory JSON
claude-code Native Claude Code JSONL
codex Native Codex rollout JSONL
copilot-cli Native GitHub Copilot CLI event JSONL
cursor Cursor role/message content-block JSONL capture
droid Native Droid session JSONL
gemini-cli Native Gemini CLI whole-session JSON
hermes Session-store message-row array or a { "session": {...}, "messages": [...] } envelope
letta-code Letta Code client transcript.jsonl
omp Native OMP (Oh My Pi) coding-agent session JSONL (pi-agent session format)
openclaw Native OpenClaw session JSONL (pi-agent session format)
opencode Native OpenCode { "info": ..., "messages": [...] } session JSON
openhands JSON event array or an events-API { "items": [...] } envelope
pi Native pi-coding-agent session JSONL
deepagents Deep Agents CLI LangGraph SQLite store plus threadId

Note: ATIF, Copilot CLI, Cursor, Gemini CLI, and OpenCode are export-only input contracts and return listing_unavailable.

🚀 Availability

The tool is available via the following packages:

  • TypeScript: Published as @letta-ai/trajectory
  • Python: Published as agent-trajectory (imported as trajectory)

For Deep Agents, normalizeCheckpoint reads sessions from its local LangGraph SQLite store by thread ID.

#AIagents #TypeScript #Python #MachineLearning

Source: letta-ai/trajectory

item.title: Multiplayer Agent Harness for Collaborative Work in Slack and Web
item.description:
Multiplayer Agent Harness for Collaborative Work in Slack and Web

A new multiplayer agent harness for work has been introduced, enabling employees to work independently in isolated workspaces or collaborate with an agent in projects, group messages, and Slack channels.

🔍 Overview

The system allows users to customize their own agent while maintaining the ability to work collaboratively. Identity and configuration are consistent between the web app and Slack. Key capabilities include:

  • Internal Search: Search across the web, databases, documents, email, and internal notes.
  • Inbox Management: Triage inboxes on a schedule with reply drafts and labels by learning a user’s writing voice from past sends.
  • Development Workflow: Work in existing repositories to monitor CI, run tests, check system logs, and open PRs.
  • Project Tracking: Post follow-ups and updates in shared channels to track projects.
  • App Creation: Build and publish custom internal apps to specific people.

🧩 How it works

Each person and room is provided with its own scoped memory, permissions, files, keychain view, durable sandbox, crons, and web apps.

  • Core Architecture: The core runs TypeScript on Node and uses Fastify for HTTP. A Postgres persistence layer manages session history, user data, and other durable state.
  • Integration: The web UI, public portal, and admin panel are optional plugins over the core’s HTTP API. Slack is an optional in-process plugin supervised through a direct service client.
  • Tooling: The agent uses a small, fixed tool surface. The execute tool allows the agent to run commands in its own isolated, durable sandbox where installed tools remain installed.
  • Tech Stack: The Slack plugin uses Bolt, while the web UI utilizes Vite for builds and Lit for rendering.
  • Vendor Neutrality: The core is driven by Pi, OpenCode, Codex, and Claude Code, meaning deployments are not tied to a single vendor.

⚙️ Key details

Administrators can set a security posture, org-level configuration, and determine available models and harnesses.

Security Posture Description
Strict Every harness tool call requires human approval, except for two no-effect turn enders.
Auto (default) A classifier screens tool results and provenance-labelled external data; deployments can use their own screening proxy.
Dangerous No pauses between tool calls and no content screening.

Regardless of the posture, a predeclared command policy applies to provide hard denials and approval rules for destructive SQL or recursive deletes.

Additional technical specifications include:

  • Deployment: Every company’s specific configuration, infrastructure, custom tools, skills, and sandbox image live in a deployment directory validated and deployed via the qm CLI. Each deployment runs in the operator’s own cloud account.
  • Skills: Skills are scope-owned and shareable by grant. Skill packs can be imported from git repositories, and admin-gated promotion to the whole org is available.
  • Automation: Inbound webhooks, watches, and crons run work independently.
  • Memory: Built-in notebooks are available, though memory can be routed by scope to external providers.

#AIagents #Slack #TypeScript #Productivity #SoftwareDevelopment

Source: yc-software/qm
